_meta.description: Per-field synthetic event coverage matrix for the REST /snapshot completeness conformance test (MYR-48). Catches the regression class where a wire field gets WS broadcast wiring but DB persistence is forgotten in the writer pipeline (the same class as MYR-41). The test enumerates every property in docs/contracts/schemas/vehicle-state.schema.json and, for each, applies the synthetic event declared here through the writer pipeline (or a direct seed for identity/derived fields), reads the row back via VehicleRepo.GetByVIN, and asserts the field is non-null on the read-back snapshot. Fields with category=expected_failure are KNOWN gaps tracked in dedicated Linear follow-ups (see each row's comment); the test surfaces them as t.Logf warnings so the gate stays green while the writer pipeline catches up.

vehicleId.comment: Opaque DB cuid. Seeded on vehicle creation by the Next.js app — never written by the telemetry writer pipeline. Test asserts Vehicle.ID != "" on the seeded row.

name.comment: User-assigned vehicle name. DB-seeded with non-empty value via seedVehicleWithCatalog. Test asserts Vehicle.Name != "".

model.comment: Vehicle model (Prisma NOT NULL). Seeded via catalog. Test asserts Vehicle.Model != "".

year.comment: Model year (Prisma NOT NULL). Seeded via catalog. Test asserts Vehicle.Year > 0.

color.comment: Exterior color (Prisma NOT NULL). Seeded via catalog. Test asserts Vehicle.Color != "".

licensePlate.comment: MYR-286: owner-entered plate on the Prisma Vehicle table (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''). Deliberately NOT a telemetry field — Tesla exposes no plate on any endpoint, proto, or stream, so no writer-pipeline path exists or should: the ONLY writer is the owner's PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/plate (rest-api.md §7.14). The seed synthetic stands in for that endpoint so the read-back through GetByVIN is still asserted. An EMPTY value in production means 'owner has not entered one', never a persistence gap, so this row must never become an expected_failure.

vin.comment: MYR-279: full VIN, sourced from Prisma Vehicle.vin and read by GetByVIN (which queries WHERE vin=$1, so it is always set on the read-back). Exposed on the owner /snapshot (owner-mask only). Test asserts Vehicle.VIN != "".

status.comment: Derived from gearPosition by deriveVehicleStatus(); persisted via UpdateStatus. DB DEFAULT 'offline'. Test asserts Vehicle.Status is one of the valid VehicleStatus enum values and not the empty string.

speed.comment: DB INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. After applying speed synthetic, expected 35.

heading.comment: GPS atomic group member. DB INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Active-group scenario applies all gps members together.

latitude.comment: GPS atomic group member. DB DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Test asserts non-zero (DB default 0 == 'no fix' per §2.3).

longitude.comment: GPS atomic group member. DB DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Test asserts non-zero.

locationName.comment: DB TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''. Populated server-side by the geocoder, not direct telemetry. VehicleUpdate.LocationName accepts the value through the writer pipeline. Empty-string-is-non-null per §1.1.

locationAddress.comment: DB TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''. Populated server-side by the geocoder via VehicleUpdate.LocationAddr. Empty-string-is-non-null per §1.1.

gearPosition.comment: Nullable in steady state (null = vehicle asleep or gear not yet reported). Active-group scenario asserts non-null after applying. Steady-state assertion exempted via nullableInSteadyState=true.

chargeState.comment: Nullable in steady state — null when vehicle has never charged. DB persisted as Vehicle.chargeState String? per MYR-41. Active-group charge scenario asserts non-null after applying.

rideShareEnabled.comment: MYR-342 owner ride-sharing switch. NOT a telemetry field and never will be: no Tesla proto, no vehicle_data field, no fieldMap entry — "this owner is lending their car out" is a MyRoboTaxi product fact, so the writer pipeline this harness exercises has no path to it BY CONSTRUCTION. Its only writer is the owner's PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/ride-share (rest-api.md §7.18). It lives as ride_share_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true on the Go-owned go_vehicle_control_state SIDE table (migration 0021) and reaches the wire via COALESCE(gcs.ride_share_enabled, TRUE) on the GetByID snapshot join. This harness reads back through GetByVIN, which does NOT join the side table, so what it observes is the Go zero value rather than the column — and for this field that zero value is false, i.e. PAUSED, a state the real read path can never produce. nullableInSteadyState is therefore true to keep the harness honest about what it can observe, NOT because the field is ever absent on the wire: /snapshot and GET /api/vehicles both always emit it. The side-table round trip is covered directly by internal/store/vehicle_ride_share_test.go and the /snapshot projection by internal/telemetry/vehicle_snapshot_handler_test.go.

setupState.comment: MYR-491 owner-facing setup state. NOT a telemetry field and never will be: no Tesla proto, no vehicle_data field, no fieldMap entry, and by construction a vehicle in any of these states is not sending frames at all — the whole point of the field is to explain a car that has NOT connected, so the writer pipeline this harness exercises can have no path to it. It is DERIVED read-time from the Go-owned go_fleet_config_attempts row (migrations 0031 + 0036) LEFT JOINed onto the GetByID snapshot read, together with the row's own `status` and `lastUpdated`, by a single server-side function shared with the GET /api/vehicles catalog row. This harness reads back through GetByVIN, which does not join that table, so what it observes is always the absent state — nullableInSteadyState is true to keep the harness honest about what it can observe, NOT because the field is ever missing on the wire: /snapshot and GET /api/vehicles both always emit the key (an explicit null when there is no claim). The join and the projection are covered by internal/store/vehicle_setup_schedule_test.go, the derivation rules by internal/telemetry/vehicle_setup_state_test.go, and the link-time seed that populates it for a brand-new owner by internal/store TestSeedFleetConfigAwaitingKey plus cmd/telemetry-server TestOwnerStreamHook_AfterLink.

teslaAccessType.comment: MYR-599 / contracts v0.39.0 — whether the account that linked this car OWNS it on Tesla's side or merely DRIVES it ("owner" | "driver"). NOT a telemetry field and never will be: no Tesla proto, no vehicle_data field, no fieldMap entry. It is an UPSTREAM ACCOUNT FACT captured once at link time from the Fleet API vehicles listing's `access_type`, so the writer pipeline this harness exercises has no path to it BY CONSTRUCTION — a car sending frames tells us nothing about who owns it. It is DERIVED read-time from the presence or absence of the Go-owned go_vehicle_driver_access row (migration 0046) LEFT JOINed onto the GetByID snapshot read, by the same one-line rule the GET /api/vehicles catalog row uses, so the two surfaces cannot name one car two different ways. PRESENCE decides: a row means "driver", no row means "owner", and Tesla's raw access_type token stays in the table for the operator question rather than reaching a consumer. This harness reads back through GetByVIN, which does NOT join that table, so what it observes is always the zero value — and for this field the zero value is the CORRECT wire answer ("owner"), which is why nullableInSteadyState is true to keep the harness honest about what it can observe rather than because the field is ever absent: /snapshot and GET /api/vehicles both ALWAYS emit it, with no omitempty, since an absent key already means "owner" to a consumer on a pre-v0.39.0 server and omitting the string would make the two cases indistinguishable. The join and the projection are covered by internal/store's driver-access round trip, the derivation and its precedence over every other setupState arm by internal/telemetry/vehicle_setup_state_test.go, the wire emission by internal/telemetry/vehicle_snapshot_handler_test.go, and the link-time write that populates it by cmd/telemetry-server TestOwnerStreamHook_AfterLink.

lastUpdated.comment: TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() — set by the writer on every UpdateTelemetry. Test asserts Vehicle.LastUpdated is non-zero AND was advanced by an UpdateTelemetry call (i.e., greater than the seed timestamp).

locked.comment: MYR-252 cabin-control read-back. Contracted + delivered live on the WS vehicle_update stream, but NOT persisted to the DB-backed /snapshot yet — the Vehicle table is Prisma-owned and column additions are a cross-repo migration tracked in MYR-253. Synthetic names a VehicleUpdate field that does not exist yet, so the writer-pipeline gap surfaces as an EXPECTED-GAP log line and the gate stays green until MYR-253 lands. MYR-269 now persists this to the Go-owned go_vehicle_control_state SIDE table (not the Prisma Vehicle table) and returns it on /snapshot via VehicleRepo.GetByID's LEFT JOIN; this MYR-48 completeness harness exercises the Vehicle-table writer pipeline via GetByVIN (no side-table join), so this row stays expected_failure here — the side-table round-trip is covered by internal/store/vehicle_control_state_test.go.

serviceEstimatedEndAt.comment: MYR-316 resolved service window. NOT a single column and NOT a telemetry field: it is COALESCE(service_etc, service_expected_end_at) over two nullable TIMESTAMPTZ columns on the Go-owned go_vehicle_control_state SIDE table (migration 0017), resolved by internal/telemetry/service_window.go and emitted ONLY while the vehicle's status is in_service. Neither column has a writer-pipeline path — service_etc comes from the Fleet API GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}/service_data on the ServiceStatusMonitor's connectivity-edge path, service_expected_end_at from the owner's PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/service-window (rest-api.md §7.16) — and the monitor physically clears both when the car leaves service. nullableInSteadyState is therefore true BY DESIGN, not as a documented gap: this harness's seeded vehicle is not in service, so null is the CORRECT read-back and an expected_failure row would misreport a working field as broken. The write/resolve round-trip is covered by the store and handler tests for vehicle_service_window.go.
